Otl Aicher, Ulm Volkshochschule poster “Realistische Weltliteratur der Gegenwart”, 1956

A square poster by Otl Aicher for the Ulm adult education centre: alternating red and black bars on pale paper, with the course text set inside them.

Source
Museum Ulm/HfG-Archiv, HfG-Ar Ai G 591 (museum-digital)

Context

The HfG-Archiv record gives Otl Aicher (1922–1991) as author, 1956, print on paper, 40.5 × 40.5 cm, and calls it a poster of the Ulm Volkshochschule for a course by Hans Werner Richter. museum-digital 2047820.

The record says that Richter, Inge Scholl, the founder of the Volkshochschule, and Otl Aicher met in November 1947 at a meeting of the “Gruppe 47”, and planned a “new school” from which the Hochschule für Gestaltung grew. museum-digital.

Observed

  • The square sheet is pale grey-beige paper, filled with flat bars of red and black that alternate.
  • On the left, eight horizontal bars of different lengths stack with even gaps. On the right, four vertical bars stand above five horizontal bars.
  • The title “Realistische Weltliteratur der Gegenwart” runs vertically up two red bars, in a bold sans-serif.
  • “Kurs Hans Werner Richter” and the lowercase word “dienstags” sit inside red bars in black type.
  • There is no image and no ornament.

Why it belongs

The poster shows the graphic side of Ulm before the product program: a modular system of bars, text placed inside the system, and two colors. It is louder than the Braun products and closer to the Swiss style, so it marks the edge of this record.

Borrow

Build a layout from bars of one width and set the text inside them.
